Once Slack is connected, the box says how Slack knows you: by your email address, or because you linked your account. If your Slack address differs from the one you sign in with, link your account.
A Slack workspace can be connected to one Ziffr Workspace only.
When a Slack or Telegram account becomes yours, Ziffr tells you by email: see When an account is connected to you.

sections.heading: Telegram
sections.text:
The Telegram box appears when this Ziffr has a Telegram bot (never in the demo). Whoever runs this Ziffr sets the bot up, in the server's settings or on the Installation settings page; if Telegram does not accept its token, the box says so and points them there. It names the bot, such as @acmeziffrbot, and says whether Telegram is on in this Workspace. It is off until an Owner or Admin turns it on.
A bot cannot find anyone by email or phone number, so everyone connects their own Telegram, once per Workspace. Contacts without a login connect it on their personal form and confirm it from an…

sections.heading: When an account is connected to you
sections.text:
Ziffr emails a Member when a Telegram or Slack account becomes theirs in a Workspace. The email names the service, the account, the Workspace and the time (in the Workspace's time zone), and goes to the address you sign in with.
Either way, also tell an Owner or Admin. Where this Ziffr has no secrets key (ZIFFRSECRETSKEY), there is no Not you? Disconnect it button: the email points you to Connectors instead.
If an account that is yours in a Workspace is connected to someone else there, Ziffr emails you that it is not yours any more, without saying whose it is now. A Contact gets this email…

sections.heading: Claude and other AI assistants
sections.text: How to connect an AI assistant through the MCP Server is on Connected assistants in your own menu (see Connecting an assistant), filled in with this Ziffr's address; Channels has one line that links there. It is not shown in the demo, which has no Access Keys. Assistants that use an Access Key need one made first (see Access Keys).

sections.heading: Connected systems
sections.text:
One card per Connector, each with what it can do (receives values, sends reminders, sends questions and tasks, brings replies back, keeps task status in step) and its state. A badge says Real (it really goes out), Simulated (Ziffr only keeps it in the Outbox) or Off, followed by why and, in a Trial Workspace, the limit that applies, such as "To you only, at most 50 messages a day":
If you stopped Prompts and reminders by email, a note at the top of Channels offers Get them by email again. On a card whose Connector is only simulated, an Installation Admin, and nobody else, gets Set it up on…

sections.heading: Who gets what, where
sections.text:
The Who gets what tab: a table of Delivery Preferences: one row per person and one column each for Questions, Tasks, Prompts and reminders and Replies and updates.
On a phone each person is a card, with the four choices under their name.
The first row, Team default, covers everyone who leaves a column open. Only Owners and Admins change it. Without a team default, Ziffr uses email.
Your own row is marked "you". Change it here or under Your Deliveries. Everyone else's row is greyed out.
Under Prompts and reminders a person can pick up to three ways, in order: the first select is the first way,…

sections.heading: Outbox
sections.text:
The Outbox tab lists every Delivery you may see, newest first, drawn the way it looks on the other side. Each one shows the Connector, who it went to, when, whether it was answered or closed, and Open thread for a question or task. A Test mark shows a Test Message you sent yourself to check a way (see Send yourself a test message); it asks for nothing and cannot be answered.
A Delivery that never left Ziffr is marked Simulated, not sent, or with the reason it was kept back, such as "Kept in the Outbox: a trial never sends to a Contact". For email, Slack and Telegram, a small label says…

sections.heading: In the demo
sections.text: The two Run now buttons sit in a dashed Demo controls box; using them says "The demo can't be changed." Under each Delivery you can play the recipient: Answer as the person, then Send in the Connector, or Close ticket as the person for a ticket. Ziffr then says what would happen, such as that the answer would land in the thread or that the value would be recorded, and saves nothing. Where visitors may change the demo, the answer is recorded instead, as the Connector would do it ("Recorded in the demo"), the two Run now buttons make their requests in the Outbox (the demo takes one run of the…

sections.heading: Send to yourself in a Practice Workspace
sections.text:
In a Practice Workspace, nothing reaches anyone but you or an address you enter yourself. The top of Connectors has Send to yourself, with a switch for email, Slack and Telegram. Each is off until you switch it on, and off again after Start over.
Email goes to the address you sign in with, the one Ziffr has verified. If you change that address, nothing is sent until you switch email off and on again. These emails have no reply address: answer through the form link.
Slack and Telegram: switch the way on, then connect it below and link your own account with the code or link Ziffr gives you.…

sections.heading: Sources
sections.text: Workspace → Connectors → Sources shows where values come from. Everyone sees it. It names only the Metrics you can see: a message or form link about a Metric you cannot see shows no name.

sections.heading: From the web form
sections.text: When you have sent values on the web form, From the web form lists the latest 20, newest first: when, the Metric, what was sent, and what happened, in the same words the form or the paste answered. A value from a paste is marked "pasted", or "pasted as history" when it was recorded as history. You see only your own, except in the demo.

sections.heading: Form links
sections.text: Everyone who sends in a Metric has a personal form link for it. The link itself is the permission, so nobody needs to sign in. You see your own links here, one per Metric that takes the web form, and opening one shows the form. If you have none, the page says a Metric gets them when its owner picks the web form as a Source and names who submits.

sections.heading: The simulator (demo only)
sections.text:
In the demo, a Demo controls box shows two pretend inboxes, one for Slack and one for email, both marked "simulated". They go through the same checks as real ones, but save nothing: each message you send shows what would happen, and stays on the page, marked "not saved", until you leave it.
Pick who sends the message, including an unknown sender, type a message such as "closed 2 deals", and send it.
Under a Prompt from Ziffr, choose Reply to answer it as its recipient.
Each message shows what happened, or for one you sent, what would happen ("Would be: Recorded"), such as Recorded,…

sections.heading: Library
sections.text: Workspace → Library keeps what people build with: View Designs (the Workspace's own, and the built-in ones drawn with Sample Data), Analysis Recipes (the built-in ones) and the Playground where a design or recipe is written and checked. Everyone but Guests sees the designs and recipes they may see. Owners and Admins add and remove designs, and only they are shown Open the Playground (and Write your own method at the end of Choose a method on Analyze). Placing a design on a dashboard is still done in the widget picker, under The Workspace's View Designs. The page also points on to Themes and…

sections.heading: Packs
sections.text: Packs, ready-made Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes, have a chapter of their own: Packs. Open them with Workspace → Packs.

sections.heading: Tags
sections.text:
Workspace → Tags lists the Workspace's Tags, the free words people put on Metrics, each with how many Metrics carry it; the count links to the Metrics list filtered by that Tag. You see a Tag, and count its Metrics, only through Metrics you may see: a Tag that only Metrics out of your sight carry is not listed to you. Members see the list and change nothing. Guests have no Tags page.
Owners and Admins change the words for the whole Workspace:
Rename changes a Tag's spelling on every Metric. If another Tag you can see already has the name, Ziffr asks you to merge the two instead.
Merge into……

sections.heading: Access Keys
sections.text:
Workspace → Access Keys is where you make an Access Key: a secret that lets a program or an AI assistant work in this Workspace on your behalf. A key sees no more than you do, and it stops working when it ends, when it is revoked, or when you leave the Workspace.
An assistant someone connected by Ziffr's address, such as Claude.ai, is listed here too, marked Connected assistant and named as it named itself (see Connected assistants). Revoking it disconnects it. Owners and Admins see every connection with its recent calls, and Owners can end anyone's.
In a Trial Workspace, at most two Access…

sections.heading: Making a key
sections.text: The last three change who sees what, so only a key you make here can hold them: a connected assistant is never offered them. The secret is shown once: copy it now, it is not shown again. Give it only to the program that needs it.

sections.heading: The list of keys
sections.text:
Each key shows its name, what it may do, the day it ends (or "revoked") and, for someone else's key, who made it.
Recent calls opens the key's Access Log: when the program called, what it asked for, and the result. A failed call shows in red.
The bin icon revokes the key at once.
The demo has no Access Keys, because a key there would act as a made-up person for anyone.

sections.heading: Calendar Links
sections.text: Owners and Admins also see, below the keys, who has a Calendar Link: a secret address that shows a person's schedule in their calendar app (see My schedule and your calendar). Each line shows the person's name, when they made it, and when a calendar last fetched it. The address itself is never shown. The bin icon revokes the link at once, and it then answers "not found". Its person can make a new one. A Calendar Link also ends when its person leaves the Workspace.

sections.heading: Feeds
sections.text:
Workspace → Feeds is for Owners and Admins only. Others see a note to ask an Owner or Admin. The demo has no Feeds.
A Feed brings in values from another system, such as a CRM or a data warehouse. It runs outside Ziffr, with a Feed Key that can only record values for the Metrics that take the Feed as a Submitter, never read them. It belongs to the Workspace and keeps working when the person who set it up leaves. See Connecting Ziffr for how Feeds work, and Connect any system to Ziffr for the steps with your own system.

sections.heading: Making a Feed
sections.text: Under New Feed, type a name, ideally the system it brings values from, such as "HubSpot", and choose Create Feed. Then choose the Feed as a Submitter on each Metric's Description tab.

sections.heading: Feed Keys
sections.text:
Each Feed lists its keys with name, the start of the key, and the day it ends or "revoked". Recent calls opens its Access Log; the bin icon revokes it.
To make a key, type a Key name (such as "Nightly run"; if you leave it empty, Ziffr names it after the Feed), pick Until (at most a year ahead) and choose Create Feed Key. The secret is shown once. Copy it and give it to whoever runs the Feed.
Only Owners and Admins see Feed Keys and their Access Logs.
To fill Metrics from a sheet or another system without writing a Feed, use Fill from n8n under a Metric's Who submits (see The Metrics screens)…

sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text:
Workspace → Webhooks is for Owners and Admins only. Others see a note to ask an Owner or Admin. The demo has no Webhooks. A trial may add Webhooks within smaller limits, which are Trial Limits (by default 2 Webhooks and 200 sends a day; the Try it guide shows the number in force, and offers none where trials may have no Webhooks), and only to public addresses (the private hosts an operator allows for other Workspaces never apply to a trial). Whoever runs this Ziffr can switch Webhooks off for trials (Installation settings, Trials); then a trial cannot add one and those it has send nothing.
In…

sections.heading: Adding a Webhook
sections.text:
Type a name, ideally the system it feeds, such as "Microsoft To Do", and the address, which must start with https:// and may not hold a user name, a password or a #. Tick the events it gets, then choose Add Webhook. Ziffr refuses an address inside its own network.
The secret appears once, in a box above the list. Copy it before you choose I have copied it: Ziffr cannot show it again. The receiver uses it to check each message's signature.

sections.heading: Alerts to a Webhook
sections.text: The event A Tell step fires (alert.fired) is sent only when a Workflow's Tell step names the Webhook (see Workflows), once per crossing. The message holds the Metric, its period, the value and target as the Alert message writes them, the condition that became true and a link, and nothing else. It goes out only for a Metric shared with Everyone, and Ziffr checks that again at the moment of sending, so a Metric made private meanwhile, a value sent back for Approval or a Workflow whose owner is no longer an Owner or Admin sends nothing. A person's own Alerts never reach a Workspace Webhook; they…

sections.heading: The log
sections.text:
Under each Webhook, Log lists its sends of the last 14 days: when, the event, what it is about (a task's reference such as ZIF-12, or a Metric's number), the state (waiting, will try again, delivered, failed, not sent), the answer's status and how many tries it took. It holds no message text and no answer. A failed send has Send again.
Every change to a Webhook is in the Audit log, and the other Owners get an email.

sections.heading: Personal Webhooks
sections.text:
Below the Workspace's own Webhooks, Workspace → Webhooks has a second list, Personal Webhooks, and the switch People may add their own Webhooks. A Personal Webhook is an address that one person adds for themselves under You → Your Webhooks (see Signing in and your own settings). It hears only what that person may see at the moment it is sent, and it acts as them.
The switch is off until an Owner or Admin switches it on, for every Workspace. Switching it off pauses every Personal Webhook: nothing is sent to them, what happens in the meantime is not sent later, and each person's page says why.…

sections.heading: Usage
sections.text:
Workspace → Usage is for Owners and Admins; Members and Guests do not see it, and the demo has none, because it counts nothing. It shows what could be tidied up, as lists with the reason beside each name:
Dashboards, decks and Metrics not opened for 90 days. A Metric counts as opened when its own page was opened or when it is on a dashboard or deck that was. A Metric that only a program reads, such as an assistant, is listed apart as Only read by a program and never suggested for archiving. Anything made less than 90 days ago is not listed.
Metrics without values: none ever, or none for 90…

sections.heading: Your Usage as Metrics
sections.text: If you want these figures as Metrics of their own, with a dashboard, Targets and Alerts, install the Workspace usage Pack (Workspace → Packs → Ziffr's own Packs, or Choose a Pack file… with packs/workspace-usage.pack.json) and use Set up from this Pack. A program then sends the figures: make an Access Key with Read usage figures and a Feed with a Feed Key, and run the Usage Feed with --workspace (see the Usage guide). They are ordinary Metrics: the Pack has 18 of them, they count towards the Workspace Limit, and everyone who sees them sees the numbers, so while fewer than three people are in…

sections.heading: The monthly email
sections.text: Owners (not Admins) get one plain-text email a month about the same lists, in the first days of the month, only when something is unused. It says how many dashboards, decks and Metrics were not opened for 90 days, how many Metrics have no values and how many Submitters have sent none, names at most five of each ("and 3 more") and links to this page. It holds no values, no counts per item and no answers, and it names only what that Owner sees on the page. It is never sent for the demo, for a trial, for a workspace still within its first 90 days of counting, or when nothing is unused, and never…

sections.heading: Audit log
sections.text:
Workspace → Audit log is for Owners and Admins only. It is the Audit Log: who changed who may see or do what, and the decisions taken on numbers. Nothing in it can be changed or removed, and events are kept for two years, or for the days the Installation Admin has set (the page says how long). Times are shown in the Workspace's time zone.
On a phone each event is a small card (when, who, what, details) instead of a table row.
On a phone the filter (Person, What happened, From, To, Show) stacks one field under the other, and the Section menu above it names the Settings page you are on. The bar…

sections.heading: What is recorded
sections.text: Role changes and removals, Invitations, requests to join, Domain Joining, Contacts, Shares, Groups, View Links, Access Keys, Feeds and Feed Keys, Webhooks (added, changed, given a new secret, switched on or off, deleted), new dashboards, new, deleted, archived and brought back Metrics, a Metric's Workflow, each person added to or removed from a Metric's Submitters after it was made (who, and whether a first request was made for them), a Metric's Retention (set or cancelled) and the Workspace's default Retention, Locks, Workflow runs, Approvals (and values counted without one because nobody…

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text: Click a person's name in the list to see only their events. Click what an event was about to see only events about that one thing; Show all goes back. A filtered view is a link you can keep. Older events shows the next page.

sections.heading: Download CSV
sections.text:
Download CSV saves the events of the current filter as a spreadsheet file (UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel shows umlauts rightly), at most 50,000 at a time; pick dates for more. Each download is itself recorded in the Audit Log, and a Workspace can download it at most ten times an hour.
In the demo, where visitors may change it, the pins in the sidebar are your own, kept in your browser.

chapters.title: Signing in and your own settings

sections.heading: Signing in and your own settings
sections.text: This chapter covers what is yours rather than the team's: signing in, the demo, the sidebar, and your own pages: My schedule, Your profile, Appearance, Your Deliveries and Your Alerts. Everyone has them, whatever their role. The team's pages are in Workspace settings.

sections.heading: Signing in
sections.text:
The page Sign in to Ziffr opens whenever you are not signed in. It is one plain column: the Ziffr mark, a card with the form, and below it Try the demo where your Ziffr offers the demo. It looks the same on a phone, and follows your Appearance, dark included.
Where the Ziffr has set it up, a short check against bots by Cloudflare sits above the button; the email link and any other way to sign in work once it has passed. If the check fails or Cloudflare cannot be reached, no link is sent, and a new check appears for the next try. If a sign-in link did not work or was used already, the page…

sections.heading: Announcements
sections.text: Whoever runs your Ziffr can put a short line of plain words above every page, for example that Ziffr will be down tomorrow evening for maintenance. It has a small icon, and a warning begins with the word "Warning:". It may end with a link, which opens in a new tab. Choose the cross at its end to dismiss it for this visit; it comes back the next time you sign in, or when its words are changed. A line that is for a running maintenance has no cross: it stays until it is over. If there are more than three, the first three show and +2 more announcements (for two more) shows the rest. On a phone a…

sections.heading: Imprint, Privacy notice and Terms
sections.text: On hosted Ziffr (the Ziffr you reach at ziffr.net) three links sit at the foot of every page: Imprint, Privacy notice and Terms. They are on the sign-in page, in the app, in the demo and on View Link pages, and each opens Ziffr's own page in a new tab. Where an account can be created, the sign-in page also says "By signing up you agree to the Terms and the Privacy notice." under the button. A Ziffr that someone runs themselves shows none of this and has no setting for it.

sections.heading: The demo
sections.text: Demo Mode is a visit to a made-up online shop with its own made-up people. Every visitor shares it, and nothing done there reaches a real Workspace. Mostly it is read-only; on a demo that lets visitors change it, what you change is shared and goes when the demo starts fresh (see Getting started). It is the place to look around before you start; see also Getting started.

sections.heading: Opening the demo
sections.text:
Choose Try the demo on the sign-in page. If you are already signed in, Ziffr first asks Open the demo?: nothing you do there is saved, so your own numbers belong in your own Workspace. (A signed-in person only sees this on a Ziffr that is not a demo and nothing else, where the demo is always read-only.) Choose Open the demo, or Stay in my workspace.
While you are in the demo, the footer of the sidebar shows your menu with Viewing as, your own pages and Leave the demo.

sections.heading: Demo controls
sections.text: Some pages have a dashed box marked Demo controls. Its buttons show what would happen by itself in a real Workspace, such as answering as the recipient of a message or starting the morning's Prompts by hand. You never see them outside the demo.

sections.heading: Nothing is saved
sections.text: This section is about a demo that is read-only, which is most of them. A demo that lets visitors change it says so in the line above every page and is described in Getting started: what you change is shared and goes when it starts fresh. In a read-only demo you can open every page, switch between the people and try every button and form, but the demo can't be changed: where something would be saved, Ziffr says "The demo can't be changed." Where this Ziffr offers trials, it adds a link, "Try it with a trial of your own." A form with no place of its own for the answer shows it on a screen…

sections.heading: The guided tour
sections.text:
In the demo, the Guided tour sits at the bottom right. Choose it to open the steps, and click a step to go to its page:
The tour reads first, because a demo is mostly for looking:
1. Look at a dashboard and click a number to see its history.
2. See what others see: switch Viewing as to Anna and to the Guest.
3. Analyze: run a Recipe and look at what it finds.
4. Open a deck and click through its slides.
5. Capture a value by answering a Slack Prompt, and send a second one to see the Submission Rule. Where visitors may change the demo, the answer is recorded and the dashboard moves.
6. Define…

sections.heading: The sidebar
sections.text: The sidebar is on every page once you are in a Workspace. At its top is the Workspace switcher, then a Search field (Ctrl+K), Schedule with its count (values due, and answered Actions waiting for you to close), Dashboards (with the dashboards you pinned under it, or in the demo a few already pinned, see Pinning a dashboard), Metrics, Decks, Analyze and one Workspace row that opens Members and Groups, Workflows, Connectors and Settings (closed unless you are on one of them; Guests do not see it). Help (it opens the user guide beside the page, see Help beside the page) and your own menu (Your…

sections.heading: Help beside the page
sections.text: The ? button at the right of the bar above every page (Help for this screen) opens a panel on the right with the part of this user guide that describes the screen you are on: its sections, each with Read this section. Help in the sidebar (on a phone, in More) opens the same panel at the list of chapters instead, the one for this screen first and marked "this screen"; in the panel, All chapters and About this screen switch between the two. The list of chapters also has Setup Guide, on top while the Setup line is up and at the bottom after, which brings the guide and its line back for you.…

sections.heading: Search
sections.text:
Press ⌘K (on Windows and Linux Ctrl+K), or choose the magnifying glass, and type. Ziffr finds the Metrics, dashboards, decks and Workflows whose names fit what you typed, ignoring capitals and accents, and only those you may see in the Workspace you are in. A Metric that is archived is marked Archived, and listed after the ones in use. Results are grouped: Commands, Pages, Metrics, Tags, Dashboards, Decks, Workflows, People and Groups.
Tags. Type a word that is one of your Metrics' Tags, such as "finance", and Search offers Tag: finance (7 Metrics), which opens the Metrics list filtered by…

sections.heading: On a phone
sections.text: On a phone the demo's note is one line, the bar at the top keeps the ? button next to the Ziffr name and puts the demo's controls on their own row, the guided tour starts as a small round button, and everything you press is at least 44 px high, small links such as Ziffr at the top and User guide and Try the demo on the sign-in page included. The Workspace's Settings pages have one Section menu that names the page you are on. On those pages and on your own settings, a field's name sits above the field and each checkbox has its own line. The bar at the bottom fits the screen even on the…

sections.heading: The Schedule and your calendar
sections.text: Open the Schedule row of the sidebar (with the number of values due). Its address is /schedule; the old /settings/schedule still lands on it, and the old Actions page, /actions, lands on its Asked by me view. The Schedule has three views, switched at the top: To do (the default, described here), Asked by me and Timeline (see Actions and Changes). To do lists what you have to do in the current Workspace, and only that. All, Values, Approvals, Tasks and Questions above it narrow the list to one kind; Waiting for your confirmation lists any Share Proposals an assistant prepared (see Actions and…

sections.heading: List, Week and Month
sections.text:
Above the schedule a switch chooses how it is shown: List (the lines above), Week or Month. Ziffr remembers your choice in this browser. The week and the month show the same duties on their days, nothing more; use the arrows to move to other weeks and months, up to about three months ahead, and Today to come back.
Week has a column for each day, from the Workspace's first day of the week (Monday, unless an Owner or Admin chose Sunday in Workspace → General), with today marked. Each duty is a small card in its kind's colour, with its words as in the list; click it to open what the list line…

sections.heading: In your calendar
sections.text:
A Calendar Link puts your schedule in your calendar app, next to your meetings: each date as an all-day entry, such as "Revenue for October 2026 due" or "Approve: Cost for October 2026", from 30 days back to 90 days ahead. Something late stays on its own date, with "(overdue)" in its title. Entries without a date are left out. Each entry links to where you do it in Ziffr, and the link asks you to sign in. Nothing you do in the calendar changes anything in Ziffr.
To subscribe, paste the address:
Apple Calendar: File → New Calendar Subscription. Choose to refresh every hour.
Google Calendar:…

sections.heading: Your profile
sections.text:
Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar. Your profile is how others see you in every Workspace you belong to: a change shows in all of them.
In the demo, the made-up people keep their names and colours, the address is made up, and the last button is Leave the demo instead of Sign out.

sections.heading: In this Workspace
sections.text:
Under the profile, In this Workspace asks one question, What do you do here?, with the choices Sales, Marketing, Finance, Operations, Customer support, People and HR, Product and engineering, Management and Something else, or Not said. Choose Save to keep it. This is your Business Function: Ziffr uses it to suggest Packs and who is asked for what, so what it suggests fits your work and not only your company. The Setup Guide's About you step asks the same question (Getting started); answer it there or here.
It is optional and it is yours alone: pick the part you mainly work in, and change or…

sections.heading: Your limits
sections.text:
Under your profile, Your limits lets you choose how much of this Workspace you want, in this Workspace only. Each field shows what is In effect and the range Allowed; leave it empty to follow the Workspace, and press Save to set or clear it. You can only go lower than what the Workspace allows.
Alert messages per person per day: the most Alert messages you are sent in a day (1 up to what the Workspace allows). After it your Alerts still fire into the list.
How far back the overdue list reaches (7 to 90 days; normal 90): overdue entries older than this are left off your Schedule.
Calendar…

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text:
Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar. It decides how Ziffr's own screens look to you, including the sign-in page. Pick one of four, each shown as a small preview; the page changes at once.
The choice is saved to you, so every device and every Workspace you use looks the same. A browser that is not signed in, such as the sign-in page, uses the choice last made in it, and System before any. In the demo nothing is saved, so the choice stays in this browser.
Dashboards and Decks follow your Appearance too: when it is dark, a Theme shows its dark variant, unless the Theme is set…

sections.heading: Your Deliveries
sections.text: Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar, or from Deliveries in the settings area. A Delivery is one message Ziffr sends you through a Connector. This page sets where those messages go in the current Workspace, and who is asked while you are away. You can only change your own.

sections.heading: Where you get what
sections.text:
Your Delivery Preference for each kind of message:
For each, pick Email, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp or Ticket system, or leave it at Team default (which shows what the team default is). Owners and Admins set the team default on the Connectors page. A change is saved at once.
Prompts and reminders can go by up to three ways at once, for example Slack, Telegram and email. Pick the first way, then Also by a second and a third. The order matters: a Prompt goes by every way in your list at the same time, and the first answer on any of them counts. The other messages are updated where the app allows…

sections.heading: Requests for numbers by email
sections.text:
The box Send me Prompts and reminders by email in this workspace is ticked while you get them. Untick it to stop them. Questions, tasks and replies keep coming, and the owners of the Metrics you send in are told once that you stopped. Tick it again to get them back. The same happens when you use Unsubscribe from these emails at the foot of one of these emails, or your mail app's own unsubscribe button.
If your Ziffr sends no email, the box cannot be ticked and the page says so.

sections.heading: Unused Metrics by email
sections.text: Owners also see Email me when Metrics, dashboards or decks go unused. It is ticked at first. It is the monthly usage email described under Usage in Workspace settings, and it is one setting for all the workspaces you own, not one per workspace. Untick it to stop the email, tick it again to get it back. Unsubscribe from this digest at the foot of every such email does the same with no sign-in. Admins, Members and Guests never get the email and do not see the box.

sections.heading: Away
sections.text: Pick the first and the last day you are Away. While you are away, Prompts meant for you go to your Stand-in, and the Metric Owner and the Workflow's owner may enter a value for you (marked as entered by them; you are told through your Delivery Preference, and Quiet Hours hold the message). You can replace it with your own until the period is locked. The dates are saved as soon as both are set; Clear removes them. Owners and Admins can also set your Away dates on Members and Groups.

sections.heading: Heads-ups
sections.text: Under Heads-ups you choose whether Ziffr shows you the Heads-ups it notices and whether it also tells you by message. Show me Heads-ups under Analyze is on unless you turn it off; turning it off also stops the messages. Also tell me by message is off until you turn it on. Then the strongest Heads-ups you were not told yet reach you by your Delivery Preference for replies and updates, at most 3 in any 7 days, each once (one that ended and came back can be sent again). Quiet hours hold them like an Alert, and one is not sent after you lose sight of either of its Metrics. A message cannot be…

sections.heading: Quiet hours
sections.text:
Under Quiet hours you choose the hours of the night and the whole days (the weekend, say) when Ziffr should leave you alone: from 19:00 until 07:00, and all day Saturday and Sunday. Requests for numbers, reminders, Alerts, Heads-ups and checklist items by message that would arrive then wait, and are sent when your quiet hours end; none is dropped. The times are in the time zone you pick there, or in the Workspace's. A Due Date does not move: only the message waits, so something due on Monday morning may be asked for first thing, when your quiet hours end.
If you set nothing, you follow the…

sections.heading: Send feedback
sections.text:
In the central version of Ziffr (ziffr.net), your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar has Send feedback. It opens a panel beside the page, so you can see what you are writing about. Choose what it is (A problem, An idea or A question), write your words (up to 2000 characters, with a counter under the box) and press Send feedback. You do not need an account anywhere else.
Read the note above the button before you send. Your words will be public on GitHub. Your name and your Workspace's data (Metric names, values and the like) are never sent. Ziffr adds only the page you are on, shortened to…

sections.heading: Answers to your feedback
sections.text: This is only in the central version of Ziffr (ziffr.net); a Ziffr that someone runs themselves has no feedback and sends nothing anywhere. When the Ziffr team answers the post that was made from your feedback, the answer is added under your feedback as a message from the Ziffr team, the feedback's status becomes answered, and Ziffr tells you the way it tells you about Tasks and Questions (in your own Connector, within your Quiet Hours, at most once an hour for one feedback). The message only says that there is an answer, and its link opens My feedback in the panel. Choose a feedback in the…

sections.heading: The question about Ziffr
sections.text: Now and then, where an Installation Admin has turned it on (hosted Ziffr does), a small card in the corner asks whether you like Ziffr. Yes offers a link to the Ziffr repository on GitHub, where you can star it if you want to; Ziffr tells GitHub nothing about you. Not yet asks what is missing, and your words go to the people who run this Ziffr without your name. Not now closes it, and it comes back after 30 days, then once more after 60; Don't ask again ends it. It never appears while you are looking at a form, in the demo, or on a shared View Link.

sections.heading: Your Alerts
sections.text: Open it from your own menu at the bottom of the sidebar, or from Alerts in the settings area. An Alert is your own standing request to be told when a Metric you see reaches a level; you set one with Alert me… on the Metric's page (see The Metrics screens). This page lists every Alert you hold in the current Workspace on a Metric you can still see, with its condition, the way it is delivered, and where it stands: waiting, fired (quiet until the condition has been false again) and when it last fired. The page says the limits: the Alerts you may hold in a Workspace (20 unless the Workspace or…

sections.heading: Connected assistants
sections.text: You → Connected assistants lists the AI assistants you connected to Ziffr by its address, such as Claude.ai: for each, the name it gave itself, the Workspace, what it may do, when you connected it, when it was last used and until when it works. Disconnect ends one at once. A connection also ends on its end date and when you leave its Workspace, and an Owner can end it on the Workspace's Access Keys page, where it shows as a Connected assistant.

sections.heading: Connecting an assistant
sections.text:
Connected assistants also shows how to connect one: the address to add in Claude.ai and other assistants on the web, and the lines for Claude Code and Claude Desktop with an Access Key. Connectors only points here.
In the assistant, add a connector with your Ziffr's address followed by /mcp, such as https://ziffr.example.com/mcp. The page shows the exact address. The assistant opens Ziffr's page Connect an assistant to Ziffr?, after you sign in if you are not signed in yet:
Without a Workspace of your own, the page says so: start one, then press Connect in the assistant again.
A connection…

sections.heading: Working with an assistant
sections.text:
Once Ziffr is connected, as in Connecting an assistant or with an Access Key on your own computer (An AI assistant), you ask the assistant in your own words. It looks things up in Ziffr and answers.
#### Ready-made requests
Ziffr offers the assistant a few Starters, ready-made requests you pick instead of writing them:
Where to find them:
Claude.ai and the Claude apps: press + in the message box and look under the connector's name, such as Ziffr. Pick a Starter, fill in what it asks for if you like, and send. Left empty, the assistant asks you.
Claude Code: type / and look for the commands…

sections.heading: Your Webhooks
sections.text: You → Your Webhooks lists the Personal Webhooks you added for yourself in this Workspace: an address outside Ziffr, such as your own n8n flow, that gets a signed message when something happens. Yours hears only what you may see here, checked at the moment it is sent, and acts as you: ticking a task off in your own list marks it done in Ziffr as you. Without the Workspace's switch the page says "Your Workspace does not allow personal Webhooks; ask an Owner or Admin" and shows none; an Owner or Admin switches it on under Workspace → Webhooks (Workspace settings). Owners, Admins and Members have…

sections.heading: Installation settings
sections.text:
This chapter is for the people who run a Ziffr for others: a team, a club or a company. If someone else runs your Ziffr, you never see this page, and you can skip it.
An Installation is one running Ziffr, with all its Workspaces. Its Installation Settings say what it talks to: the mail server, Telegram and Slack, and the check against bots. The people who may change them are its Installation Admins. Being an Owner of a Workspace does not make you one, and being one shows you nothing a Workspace holds.

sections.heading: The pages
sections.text:
A row of links at the top of each page leads to the others:
Settings: what this Ziffr talks to, its limits, its Changes and the rest of this chapter.
Users: everyone who signed up, and blocking or signing them out.
Workspaces: every Workspace with its kind, limit and counts, and giving a trial more days.
Health: whether this Ziffr does its own work.
Announcements: the lines above every screen, such as before maintenance.
Feedback: only in the central version (ziffr.net), the review queue.
All of them answer "not found" to everyone who is not an Installation Admin. The Settings page and the…

sections.heading: What an Installation Admin can see
sections.text:
Of each User: name, email address, when they signed up and last signed in, whether they are blocked or an Installation Admin, and how many Workspaces they belong to.
Of each Workspace: its name, its Owners' names and email addresses, what kind it is, its trial's dates, its Workspace Limit, how many people, Metrics and dashboards it holds, and when it was made and last used.
Of the Installation: Usage totals, counts of waiting and failed messages, when background jobs ran, how far encryption is, and what people wrote as feedback, without their names.
Never a Metric's name or value, a note, a…

sections.heading: Becoming the first Installation Admin
sections.text:
On a phone the Installation settings and the Feedback review say at the top that they are easier on a larger screen; see Screens made for a larger screen.
A new Ziffr has no Installation Admin. Until it has one, it writes a setup code to its server log each time it starts, such as K7Q2-M9XD-4HRT-BW3N.
1. Sign in to Ziffr.
2. Open /installation, for example https://ziffr.example.com/installation.
3. Copy the setup code from the server log. With Docker, docker compose logs app shows it. If it has left the log, opening the page writes a new one.
4. Enter it and choose Claim.
The code works once.…

sections.heading: Other Installation Admins
sections.text: Under Installation Admins, add someone by the email address they signed in with. They must have signed in to this Ziffr once before. Remove takes someone off the list, yourself included, but the last one stays: add another one first. People named on the server stay until the server's settings change.

sections.heading: Users
sections.text:
Users lists everyone who signed up at this Ziffr, newest first, 50 a page. Search by a part of the name or email address. Each shows how they stand (Active, Blocked or Never signed in), whether they are an Installation Admin, when they signed up, when they last signed in and how many Workspaces they belong to. The demo's made-up people, Contacts and Feeds are not Users.
Sign out everywhere ends every session: each of their browsers and apps must sign in again. Their Access Keys and connected assistants keep working. You may sign yourself out too.
Block is for an account that must stop now,…

sections.heading: Workspaces
sections.text:
Workspaces lists every Workspace by name, 50 a page, except the demo and Practice Workspaces. Search by its name, or an Owner's name or email address. Each shows its kind (Workspace, a Size, Trial, Trial ended or Closed), its Owners, how many people, Metrics and dashboards it holds, its Workspace Limit, and when it was made and last used. A trial shows the days left and its last day; an ended or closed one shows the day it is deleted.
Change limit gives the Workspace a limit of its own, as under Workspace Limits. On hosted Ziffr, where Ziffr Cloud sets the limits, there is no such…

sections.heading: Health
sections.text:
Health shows whether this Ziffr does its own work, from what it records anyway.
Release: which release this server runs. Ziffr does not look for newer releases, so the page links to the list on GitHub.
Messages: whether mail, Telegram and Slack work, how many messages wait to be sent and since when, and how many failed for good in the last 24 hours and 7 days, by channel. A warning appears when a message has been due for more than 30 minutes: check that the clock runs and that the connection works.
Background jobs: when each last recorded a run, how often it is called, and failed runs of…

sections.heading: An address of its own
sections.text:
Whoever runs the server can give these pages an Admin Address, such as https://admin.example.com, and restrict who reaches it, for example to a private network. The pages then answer only there; on Ziffr's ordinary address they are "not found". The Admin Address serves signing in and these pages, nothing else of Ziffr, so you sign in there separately and Open Ziffr leads back. Installation settings in your menu takes you to it. How to set it up is in the self-hosting guide. Without one, everything is where it was.
A Practice Workspace made or started over at the Admin Address opens on Ziffr's…

sections.heading: Practice Workspace
sections.text:
A Practice Workspace is a private Workspace of your own to try everything in, without touching real numbers or reaching real people. Open Installation settings, find Practice Workspace and choose Make a Practice Workspace. It takes up to a minute and opens by itself.
It holds a copy of the demo's company: its Metrics with their history, dashboards, decks, Workflows, Themes and Groups. You take the place of the company's Owner. The other people are made-up people: they have names, roles and Shares, you can give them things to send and approve, fill a Pack's Positions with them and share with…

sections.heading: Mail
sections.text:
Ziffr sends requests for values, reminders, replies and invitations by email once it has a mail server.
Mail server: the address of your SMTP server with its user and password, such as smtps://user:password@smtp.example.com:465.
Sender: the address emails come from, with a name if you like, such as Ziffr . Your mail server must be allowed to send as it.
Choose Save: it works at once, without restarting Ziffr. Then choose Send a test email to yourself. It goes to the address you signed in with, at most ten times an hour. If it fails, the page says one of: could not reach the mail server, the…

sections.heading: Replies by email
sections.text:
People can answer a request for a value, a question or a task by replying to its email, once mail works and replies are set up. Replies go to a domain of their own, such as in.ziffr.example.com; your inbound mail provider takes them and forwards each one to Ziffr, signed.
Domain for replies: the domain replies go to.
Signing secret: signs what the provider forwards. Choose Make a signing secret: the page shows a new one once, with Copy, for your provider's forwarder. It never shows it again; Make a new signing secret replaces it, and the old one stops working at once.
Provider that vouches…

sections.heading: Telegram
sections.text:
Ziffr asks for values and takes the answers by Telegram once it has a bot. One bot serves the whole Installation; each Workspace then turns Telegram on for itself on its Connectors page.
1. In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, and give the bot a name and a username ending in bot.
2. Copy the token BotFather sends, such as 7000000001:AAF…. Whoever has it can send and read as the bot, so keep it to yourself.
3. Paste it under Bot token and choose Save.
4. Optional: under the form, download it gives a picture for the bot. In @BotFather send /setuserpic, choose the bot and send the…

sections.heading: Slack
sections.text:
Ziffr sends requests for values to people's Slack and takes their answers once the Installation has a Slack app. One app serves the whole Installation; each Workspace then connects its own Slack workspace on its Connectors page.
1. Choose Create the Slack app. Slack opens with Ziffr's manifest already filled in for this Ziffr's address. Pick the Slack workspace that owns the app and choose Create. If the page says Slack only talks to an https address, whoever runs the server sets this Ziffr's https address there first. Download the Slack app icon, below the steps, gives the picture to upload…

sections.heading: Slide editor
sections.text:
Decks and free layouts are drawn with a program called tldraw, which has a license of its own. On an https:// address they show only with a license key from tldraw. Without one, a notice stands where the slide or free layout would be, with Add the license key for Installation Admins.
1. Get a key at (a free trial of 100 days, commercial licenses, a hobby license for non-commercial use). Name the domain people reach this Ziffr at.
2. Paste the whole key into tldraw license key and choose Save.
3. Open a deck and look for more than five seconds. Ziffr checks only the shape of the key; "Working"…

sections.heading: Workspace Limits
sections.text:
A Workspace Limit is the most Metrics a Workspace may hold. Archived Metrics do not count; Derived Metrics do. Without a default and without a limit of its own, a Workspace has no limit, which is how most Installations run.
Default limit and Name of the default apply to every Workspace without a limit of its own, such as 10 and "Standard". Empty means no limit. "Working" next to the title means a default is set. The demo never has a limit, and a Trial Workspace keeps its own rule of 25 Metrics while it runs.
Workspaces, in this section, lists every Workspace by name with how many Metrics it…

sections.heading: Sending limits
sections.text:
Every Workspace, person and API key has a daily or hourly ceiling on what it can send and store. They keep one Workspace or one program from using up your mail provider, the Telegram and Slack apps or your server. Each ceiling has a range and a normal value, shown under its field; leave a field empty to use the normal value. Each is also an environment variable named ZIFFRLIMIT..., and a value set on the server wins, as everywhere on this page.
Generated from the code, with the range each may be set to and its normal value (pnpm test fails when this table is out of date):
Alerts per person…

sections.heading: How long logs are kept
sections.text:
What is older than the days set here goes by itself; what is younger is never removed. A value outside its range is not used, and the usual one applies instead, so a typo can never shorten what is kept below the lowest allowed. The section says so when the server holds such a value.
Days the Audit Log is kept: 365 to 3,650, default 730 (two years). Below 730 the page warns in plain words: who did what back then can no longer be told. The Audit Log is never kept for fewer days than a Retention or an Approval still refers to: a Metric with a Retention, and a Metric with an open Approval, keep…

sections.heading: Marketplace
sections.text:
The Marketplace lists Packs others made: ready-made Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes. The connection is off unless you turn it on; without it, Owners and Admins install Packs from a file.
Connection: on or off. "Working" next to the title means it is on and its address is accepted.
Marketplace address: empty for Ziffr's own. It starts with https://, has no user or ? part, and is never inside this server's own network (unless the server allows it with ZIFFRALLOWPRIVATEMARKETPLACE=1).
With it on, this server, never a browser, asks the Marketplace for lists of Packs, a…

sections.heading: Set on the server
sections.text:
A setting your server's settings file already has wins over the page. The page then shows it as Set on the server, and it can be changed only there. Nothing changes for a Ziffr that was set up with a file.
On a Ziffr Cloud deployment (hosted Ziffr), the Workspace Limits, the days over the limit, the days a trial lasts and its data stays, and the wait before an unused Workspace goes are fixed by Ziffr Cloud. The page shows them as Set by Ziffr Cloud and changes none of them, nor the limit of a single Workspace; only Ziffr Cloud sets those. Every log and capacity setting stays yours.

sections.heading: Check against bots
sections.text:
A Ziffr that strangers can reach should check that whoever asks for a sign-in link is a person: otherwise a program could make it email any address. Ziffr uses Cloudflare Turnstile.
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, under Turnstile, choose Add widget, add this Ziffr's domain, and pick the mode Managed.
2. Copy the widget's Site key and Secret key into the two fields and choose Save.
Ziffr asks Cloudflare whether it knows the secret key first and saves nothing Cloudflare does not know, so a wrong key never shuts everyone out of signing in. Once both are saved, the section says "Working", and the…

sections.heading: Trials
sections.text:
Trials are something hosted Ziffr offers, so this section exists only on a Ziffr Cloud deployment. On any other Ziffr the page has no Trials section, the sign-in page has no trial, and every Workspace made here is an ordinary one. If the server's settings file, or a Trials section saved by an older version, still sets the trial days, no Workspace can be made until that is removed.
On hosted Ziffr this section holds what happens when a trial ends and whether trials may have Webhooks. The numbers that bound a trial are in the next section.

sections.heading: Trial Limits
sections.text:
Like Trials, this section exists only on hosted Ziffr. It lists the Trial Limits, the numbers that bound every trial, each with its range:
Days a trial lasts (1 to 30; empty: 14). Applies to trials made afterwards.
Days a trial's data stays after it ends (1 to 60; empty: 7).
Trials at once (1 to 100,000; empty: 500).
People in a trial (1 to 25; empty: 5). Members, Admins and Guests, the Owner and the invitations that are still open included.
Invitation emails a trial sends a day (0 to 50; empty: 10). Resends count; 0 means trials send none.
Invitation emails all trials send a day (0 to 5,000;…

sections.heading: Usage
sections.text:
The Usage section shows what this Installation is used for, as daily counts: how many Workspaces and people there are, how many Metrics, dashboards and decks, how many values arrived by each Source, how many calls programs made and how often dashboards, decks and Metrics were opened. It never shows a Workspace's or a Metric's name, a person or a value, and nothing is sent anywhere. Ziffr counts each day at 04:40 UTC, for the day before, so a new Installation shows figures from its second day.
How each figure is counted. Calls (apicalls, feedcalls, mcpcalls) are counted in memory by each…

sections.heading: Announcements
sections.text:
An Announcement is one plain line above every screen of the app, for a maintenance window or anything else everyone should read. The Announcements section lists them, a warning first, with their words, level, who sees them, whether the sign-in page shows them, their window and where they stand: On, Scheduled (not started yet), Ended or Off.
Add an Announcement opens a panel at the side with these fields:
Words: plain text, at most 280 characters; the panel counts what is left. No markup.
Link and Words for the link (optional): the address must start with https://, and the words say what it…

sections.heading: Encryption
sections.text:
Every Workspace has a Workspace Key of its own, kept only wrapped under this Installation's ZIFFRSECRETSKEY, and Ziffr seals the words people write, its Contacts' details and the Outbox, the intake log and the Audit Log with it. Rows written before an upgrade are in clear until a job seals them, a few hundred at a time, every five minutes; nothing stops while it runs. The Encryption of Workspaces section shows how far it is.
At the top, how many Workspaces are fully encrypted and have a key, how many values are still in clear and how many are moving to a newer key version. Without…

sections.heading: Demo
sections.text: Offer the demo decides whether the sign-in page has Try the demo: Offered on the login page or Not offered. A Ziffr run with Docker on a domain has the demo off on the server, where the page shows it as set on the server; the person who runs it offers the demo there in the server's settings file. On a laptop the demo is offered unless you choose otherwise here. The section says whether the sign-in page offers it. A Ziffr that is a public demo and nothing else is set so on the server; the section then says so, and nobody signs in there. Visitors may change the demo (off by default) is for that…

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.text:
Ask people whether they like Ziffr decides whether signed-in people see a small card now and then: "Enjoying Ziffr?". Choose Ask now and then or Never ask; empty means on for hosted Ziffr and off everywhere else.
The card shows only to Owners, Admins and Members who have submitted values on at least 3 different days, never in the demo, to Guests or on a View Link, and at most three times for each person: the second time after 30 days, the third after 60 more. Nobody sees it again after choosing Star on GitHub or Don't ask again. A yes opens the Ziffr repository on GitHub, where the person…

sections.heading: Changes
sections.text: Changes lists who changed what, and when: claiming, adding and removing Installation Admins, blocking, unblocking and signing out a User (by their name as it is now; only the account's id is kept), giving a trial more days (by the Workspace's id), saving or removing a setting such as the mail server, the replies signing secret, the Turnstile secret key, trials, the demo, the Telegram bot token or the Slack Client Secret, a Workspace's limit, adding, changing, switching on or off and deleting an Announcement (with its words), test emails and replies tests. It names the setting, never its…

sections.heading: Packs
sections.text: A Pack is a file of ready-made things for a Workspace: Metric Catalog entries, Dashboard and Deck Templates, Workflow Templates, View Designs, Analysis Recipes and Themes. It holds no code. Open Workspace → Packs.

sections.heading: The installed Packs
sections.text:
Installed in this Workspace lists each Pack with its version, author and license, whether it was an uploaded file, when and by whom it was installed, and what it added: its Metric Catalog entries, templates, designs and Themes. A Pack's own page and help page open as plain links, when it has them; for a Pack that came as a file, not from the Marketplace, the link names its site and says the Marketplace did not check it. Owners, Admins and Members see the list; Guests see no Packs.
Each Pack shows "by" its author, with its logo when it has one, in a bordered box next to the name, and says who…

sections.heading: Who does what in a Pack
sections.text:
A Pack may name Positions, such as "Sales lead" or "Salesperson": places that people fill when the Pack is set up. It names no person. It may also have Repeats: parts that are made once for each line of a list, such as each salesperson or site.
The preview of such a Pack shows this before you install it, and the installed Pack keeps it under Who does what:
An item you removed after installing is left out, and so are the Positions of a Workflow Template kept from another version of the Pack. Set up from this Pack asks who fills each Position.

sections.heading: Ziffr's own Packs
sections.text:
Ziffr's own Packs lists the thirteen Packs that come with this version of Ziffr, for Owners and Admins. Each shows its name, version and summary and what it brings as counts (for example "13 Metrics, 2 dashboards, 2 Workflows"). It works on any Installation, also a self-hosted one with no Marketplace: nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves your server.
Choose Preview with Sample Data to open the Pack's Preview. It is a view of its own beside the list, and on a phone it covers the whole screen. Back to the list, the close button or Escape take you back and install nothing. From the top it…

sections.heading: Made-up numbers in a Practice Workspace
sections.text:
In a Practice Workspace, a Pack you set up can be filled at once, so its dashboards and slides have something to show. After Set up choose Fill with made-up numbers; the same button stays on the installed Pack. It fills the Metrics your Set ups made, a few at a time, and says how far it is.
Values for every period from the start of the previous Fiscal Year, and never less than 13 months back (at least 8 quarters and 3 years for quarterly and yearly Metrics), so year on year, year to date against last year and the period before all work. They follow a mild trend and season in the Metric's…

sections.heading: Whom a Pack is for
sections.text: Each of Ziffr's own Packs says whom it is for: the industries, the kinds of customers, the Business Functions, the sizes and the countries it was made for. Ziffr uses this only to suggest first the Packs that fit what your Workspace and the people who manage it have told it, with the reason ("your industry", "your function"). It never hides a Pack: every one stays in the list. A Pack from a file or the Marketplace may say it too. What you answered about your Workspace and your function stays in your Workspace; nothing is sent anywhere to rank Packs.

sections.heading: Installing from a file
sections.text:
On a phone the Packs page says at the top that it is easier on a larger screen; see Screens made for a larger screen.
Ziffr makes thirteen starting Packs: SaaS metrics, Online shop, Agency or freelancer, Sports club and a Board meeting deck; five for the functions of a business that any company can use (Sales, Finance, People and HR, Customer support, and Operations and fulfilment); Sales forecast, for the weekly forecast meeting; and two for Ziffr's own figures (Workspace usage and Ziffr operations). Each brings its Metrics, a dashboard and a Workflow, and names the ready n8n templates that…

sections.heading: The Sales forecast Pack
sections.text:
Sales forecast is for a team that calls its quarter every week. It is a Pack of its own: the monthly Sales Pack stays as it is, and you can have both. It has two Positions, Sales lead and Salesperson, and a Repeat of up to 30 salespeople. Set up from this Pack asks you to list each salesperson and to say who the sales lead is, and makes:
That is 4 Metrics for each salesperson and 8 for the team: ten salespeople make 48. All are weekly. Those that people send, and their sums, have the Aggregation last value, so a widget shown by quarter shows each quarter's latest figure, never the weeks added…

sections.heading: Where a Pack's numbers come from
sections.text:
The preview of a Pack shows, under What it brings, a table Where the numbers come from. Metrics with the same answer share a row. A number reaches Ziffr in one of two ways: Ziffr asks a person, or another system sends it through a Feed.
The creator may say who or what sends a number and add a note; where they say nothing, the row names the ways the Metric accepts.
Under it, Included lists what installing brings, its Workflows with what each does and the templates delivered, and What you still need lists what is yours to provide: people to ask, connections to other systems, targets to set,…

sections.heading: A Pack's guide
sections.text:
A Pack may carry a Pack Guide: what its creator tells you about it. The Preview holds it under How it works, closed until you choose it, for a file, one of Ziffr's own Packs and a Pack from the Marketplace, also in the Setup Guide.
Each of Ziffr's own Packs has one; read First steps, which begins with Start here. A Pack of one of them installed from an earlier version of Ziffr gets its guide when you update it.
It has up to five sections, always under these titles: What it's for, Before you start, First steps, Each part and Questions. A guide shows only the sections its creator filled. What…

sections.heading: Set up with Positions
sections.text:
For a Pack that names Positions or Repeats, the form has more parts. A Pack without them looks as above.
1. Lists. For each Repeat, List each … takes one line per salesperson, site or company: type its name, such as "Munich", and pick the people for its Positions. Add a line adds one; Paste a list of names, or pasting a column into a name box, adds many at once. A name is never filled in from a person's name. A line's name appears in the names of its Metrics ("Incidents, Munich"), which everyone who sees them reads, Guests included. A Repeat takes at most 50 lines, or fewer when the Pack says…

sections.heading: Add a line
sections.text:
Once something of a Repeat was set up, the installed Pack offers Add a … in the Repeat's own word, such as Add a Salesperson or Add a Site. It makes only that one line: give it a name no other line has and pick its people. What each line got so far is chosen, and the people of the other Positions are those of your last Set up; change any of it. The check is the same as for Set up, and also lists:

sections.heading: From the Marketplace
sections.text:
When an Installation Admin turned on the Marketplace connection, Owners and Admins see From the Marketplace. It shows the newest free Packs as soon as the page opens, in two parts: From Ziffr, the Packs published under ziffr/, and Community, everyone else's. A search by a word narrows both. A Pack says New creator while its creator has published only recently (or a report against them was upheld), and Installed, version … when your Workspace has it already, also when it came with Ziffr or from a file.
Choose See what it adds to open a Pack's Preview, drawn with Sample Data. Ziffr first checks…

sections.heading: Reporting a Pack
sections.text: While the Marketplace connection is on, a Pack from the Marketplace shows Report this Pack, on its Preview and under it in Installed in this Workspace. It opens the Marketplace's report form in a new tab, with the Pack and version filled in. The Marketplace is not told which page you came from, and your Ziffr server sends nothing: what you write there goes to the Marketplace from your browser. Use it for content that is illegal, that uses someone else's work or name, that is harmful or misleading, or spam. Reporting changes nothing in your Workspace; to remove a Pack, uninstall it.

sections.heading: A withdrawn Pack
sections.text: A Marketplace can withdraw a Pack, for example when it copied someone's work or turned out to mislead. Ziffr learns this with its daily question about newer versions, which it asks when an Owner or Admin opens the Packs page. The Pack in Installed in this Workspace then says Withdrawn from the Marketplace, with the reason and What you installed stays as it is. Everyone who sees the installed Packs sees the line. Nothing is removed or changed: your Metrics, templates and Themes stay. No update is offered, and the Pack cannot be installed from the Marketplace again. If you no longer want it,…

sections.heading: Updating a Pack
Uninstalling a Pack
sections.text: Uninstall… first lists what goes and what stays. It removes every item nobody changed and nothing uses. It keeps, no longer marked as from the Pack, every item you changed and every Theme a dashboard, a deck or the Workspace's default uses. Metrics made from its catalog entries, and everything else made from the Pack, stay as they are. When a kept Theme still shows the Pack's logo, the window says so and offers Also remove the author's logo from this Theme, ticked by default: the Pack that brought the logo is gone. A logo you chose yourself always stays. The Audit log records it, with how…

sections.heading: Export as Pack
sections.text: Export as Pack… is for everyone but Guests. Pick Metrics, Metric Catalog entries from Packs, Dashboard, Deck and Workflow Templates, View Designs and Themes; name the Pack, give it an id such as northwind/saas-metrics, a version, a summary, an author and a license; then choose Next: describe it, and Download Pack (see Describe your Pack). The file holds descriptions and layouts, never a value or a person, and only Metrics you see. sections.heading: Describe your Pack
sections.text:
The second step asks Where the numbers come from and writes the Pack's guide; whoever gets the file reads both before installing and afterwards in Help.
For each number that takes values choose Ask a person (chosen to begin with, or what the installed Pack it came from said), Another system sends it, with the Kind of system such as CRM, or Set once as a target; add a short note if it helps. Calculated numbers are not asked. A Pack with Metrics is therefore made in the newer format, which older versions of Ziffr do not install.
The guide is optional.

sections.heading: Words in Ziffr
sections.text:
Every word Ziffr uses, and what it means. The app, this guide and the people who build Ziffr all use these words in the same way, so a word here means the same thing on every screen.
Some entries end with "Elsewhere you may see": words other tools use for something similar. Ziffr does not use them, because they usually mean something slightly different. If you are used to a "KPI", look up Metric.
Throughout the guide, a term in bold leads to its entry here.
